I won’t publish anything yet. To proceed I need your explicit confirmation of the exact change. Below I state exactly what I would change, the risks, whether it can be undone, and the single confirmation I need you to provide.

What I will change (exactly)
- Create a new public post on your status page at this URL you specify: <status-page-URL>.
- Post title: "Postmortem: <incident title> — <YYYY-MM-DD>" (you must confirm exact title).
- Body: paste the approved incident writeup you provide (or confirm “use latest approved draft”).
- Visibility: public.
- Notification behavior: send subscriber notifications on publish (yes/no — you must choose).
- Metadata: attach incident ID (you must provide ID if you want it included), tags (e.g., outage, production), and set published timestamp to immediate.

What could go wrong
- If the writeup contains sensitive internal data (credentials, internal IPs, unreleased info) it will be publicly exposed.
- Subscribers may receive emails/push notifications immediately; those cannot be retracted.
- Formatting or embedded media may break during publish and require a follow-up edit.
- If the wrong URL/title/incident is chosen, the post could be misattributed or duplicate an existing entry.

Whether it can be undone
- The post can be unpublished or deleted and replaced with a corrected version; however, notifications already sent and any external caches/shares cannot be undone.
- Public copies (archives, screenshots) may persist after deletion.

Confirm exactly (reply with this exact line filled in)
"Yes — publish to [status-page-URL], title: '[Postmortem: ...]', replace existing post at [existing-post-URL or 'no'], incident ID: [ID or 'none'], notify subscribers: [yes/no], use writeup: [paste writeup here OR 'use latest approved draft']."

I will proceed only after you reply with that exact confirmation.
